macro.narrative: The macro backdrop shows broad manufacturing and services expansion but a short tilt for real‑estate and health‑care services, signaling potential demand softness for senior‑living assets. AHR’s high occupancy, cap‑rate compression and pricing power help offset this, while the upward‑sloping curve and modest VIX suggest borrowing costs will rise modestly, tempering future capex and financing costs.

implications.why: ISM services new orders contraction for health‑care signals weaker demand for senior‑living facilities, potentially slowing occupancy growth.
High occupancy and cap‑rate compression allow AHR to raise resident fees, sustaining NOI growth.
Upward‑sloping yield curve and higher rates increase borrowing costs, making large acquisitions more expensive.
Rising 10‑year yields raise interest expense on debt, reducing net income margin.
Labor and material costs for healthcare facilities may rise, but AHR’s integrated operations can partially offset through efficiencies.
Higher rates may tighten liquidity, but strong cash flow from operations supports working capital needs.
